commitments.ndc_target: Peak CO2 emissions before 2030 and cut net GHG emissions 7–10% from peak by 2035 (first absolute target in an NDC)
key_laws: Ecological and Environmental Code (2026) — first comprehensive codification of environmental law
Dual-control on carbon emissions intensity and total (2024 reform)
Law on the Prevention and Control of Soil Pollution (2018)
Revised Forest Law (2020) — tightened logging permits, raised penalties

climate.rationale: World's largest annual emitter at ~15 GtCO2e but CO2 has been flat-to-falling for 21 months on record solar/wind build-out. 2035 NDC is the first absolute target China has ever submitted, yet the 7–10% cut from peak falls far short of a 1.5°C-compatible pathway (CAT: Highly insufficient). Coal still 55% of electricity despite renewables at 42%.

forests_land.rationale: Forest cover rose from ~12% (1949) to ~24% today via the Grain-for-Green and Three-North Shelterbelt programs — the largest afforestation effort in human history. But much of it is monoculture plantation (low biodiversity), and primary/old-growth forest continues to be lost in the southwest. 2020 Forest Law tightened protections.

biodiversity.rationale: Megadiverse (17-country list) with giant pandas, snow leopards, Yangtze finless porpoises, but under severe pressure: Yangtze baiji declared functionally extinct (2006), 21% of vertebrates threatened. 10-year Yangtze fishing ban (2021) is showing early recovery signals. Red List trajectory remains negative. [Planet Lens v1.1] Score = 80% Biodiversity Intactness Index (45.9%, NHM 2020, area-weighted) + 20% Red List Index (0.72, IUCN/OWID 2024).

protected_areas.rationale: Terrestrial protected areas at 15.61% and marine at 4.82% — well below the GBF 30×30 target adopted in Kunming on China's home soil. National Park system launched 2021 (5 parks) is a major structural step but coverage remains thin. Zero OECMs reported.

pollution.rationale: PM2.5 has fallen ~40% since the 2013 'war on pollution' but population-weighted exposure still ~30 µg/m³ (6× WHO guideline). Water quality improving; soil contamination remains a legacy problem from the industrial era. Plastic waste generation world-leading; 2020 single-use plastics ban is partially enforced.

agriculture.rationale: Highly intensive: ~35% of global synthetic fertilizer use on ~9% of global cropland, driving massive N/P runoff. Organic agriculture <1% of land. Pesticide use starting to decline from 2015 peak. Food self-sufficiency pressure conflicts with regenerative transition.

env_governance.rationale: Strong top-down capacity: Ministry of Ecology and Environment has teeth, and the 2026 Environmental Code is a milestone. But civil society and independent monitoring are heavily constrained — journalists and NGOs documenting pollution face harassment, and environmental defenders are largely invisible in global databases. Climate litigation exists but constrained.

recent_actions.action: Ecological and Environmental Code adopted — first comprehensive codification of environmental law, giving net-zero pledge statutory force
Submitted 2035 NDC — first absolute emissions target in Chinese climate pledge history (7–10% cut from peak)
Solar + wind capacity surpasses coal for the first time in installed capacity terms
Approved 6 new coal power plants totaling 8.4 GW despite renewable surge — 'coal as backup' framing continues
Yangtze fishing ban extended and expanded after early signs of finless porpoise population recovery
Launched pilot national carbon market expansion to cover cement, aluminum, and steel sectors

context.key_tension: The world's largest emitter is also the world's largest builder of renewables — whether China's energy transition reaches scale in time depends less on technology and more on whether coal is allowed to retire, not just be supplemented.
